title: bls12-381-fixed-g1-invert-g2: Special Tower Number Field Sieve (STNFS) over h(Y) = Y^6 - 2Y^3 + 2 with unfiltered Block-Wiedemann and 9x relation oversampling

claims.statement: For uniform nonidentity P in G1 and uniform z in GT on BLS12-381, the Special Tower Number Field Sieve (STNFS) attack in proof.md computes g = e(P, Q0) in GT, recovers a in [0, r) satisfying g^a = z in F_{p^12}^* using the degree-6 tower h(Y) = Y^6 - 2*Y^3 + 2 with f_y(X) = X^12 - 2*y*X^10 + 2*y^3*X^6 + y^5*X^2 + 2*y^3 - 2 and g_y(X) = X^2 - u*y at parameters A = 1024 and B = 2^65.316, and returns Q = [a]Q0 in G2 satisfying e(P, Q) = z. Because w^12 - 2*w^6 + 2 = h(w^2) is the irreducible defining polynomial of F_{p^12} and p == 3 (mod 8), h(Y) is provably irreducible modulo p and Norm_{F_{p^6}/F_p}(u*y) = 2*u^6 is a quadratic non-residue modulo p, so g_y(X) = X^2 - u*y is provably irreducible over F_{p^6} and X^(p^6) = -X. Under the STNFS smoothness, sparse-rank, and special-q descent heuristics disclosed and empirically calibrated in proof.md and experiment.py, the attack succeeds with probability at least 0.40 over uniform challenges and fresh algorithm coins (with an oversampling ratio lambda_orb / SP_orb >= 8.5 that preserves P(RF >= SP_orb) > 0.40 even under an 80% / 5x systematic downward error in mean smoothness probability) using at most 2^124.510000 total target-group-operation equivalents (normalized by C = 20,000 scalar AArch64 instructions per reference dense F_{p^12} multiplication, corresponding to at most 2^138.788940 scalar AArch64 instructions, charging unfiltered flt = 1 Block-Wiedemann linear algebra without merge-filtering assumptions). Peak memory is at most 2^76.000000 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^124.510000 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in total work; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes (2^0 bytes) and is included in memory.

experiments.purpose: Machine-check Rabin irreducibility of h(Y) = Y^6 - 2Y^3 + 2 mod p and non-residuosity (u*y)^((p^6-1)/2) == -1 mod (p, h(y)) on the exact 381-bit BLS12-381 prime p, verify exact integer norms via K_2 = Q(i) against the 3 complex conjugate-pair embeddings, observe simultaneous (N_f, N_g) smooth relations on a scaled instance to calibrate Murphy's E-function, run Algorithm 6.1 with ideal coprimality at A = 1024 and B = 2^65.316 using a strictly positive Dickman rho integral solver, and audit the unfiltered (flt = 1) instruction and memory ledgers.
